method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Coroners Act 1996 (WA), compilation from legislation.wa.gov.au (mrdoc 47642, retrieved 2026-09-07; compilation table to the Aboriginal Heritage Legislation Amendment and Repeal Act 2023 s 27, in force 15 Nov 2023; State Superannuation (Transitional and Consequential Provisions) Act 2000 s 36(2) uncommenced and not reflected), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_47642.txt; Coroners Regulations 1997, version 03-v0-00 in force from 1 July 2026 (law_s4371, mrdoc_49623, retrieved 2026-10-21), as deposited at ../../../coroners-regulations-1997/registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_49623.txt: they prescribe no circumstances for s 3 limb (d) or s 22(1)(f) and do not vary s 37(5); regs 15, 17, 22, 22A, 23B and Schedule 3 item 2 used

checks.command: l4 run cor-deaths.l4 ; l4 run cor-cases-deaths.l4 ; l4 run cor-qa.l4 ; l4 run cor-qa-cases.l4 ; l4 check cor-qa.l4
checks.result: 297 assertions satisfied (58 baseline + 239 Q&A layer), 0 errors, 0 warnings in all four files; l4 check cor-qa.l4 succeeds (2026-11-06)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: s 3 (reportable death, Western Australian death), ss 3A, 3B, 17(1), (3)-(5), 18(1), 19(1), 19A(1)-(3), 20(1), 22, 23(2), 24, 25(4), 26A, 29(1)-(3), 30, 35, 36(3) as it bears on s 29, 37(1)-(5), 44(1)-(3); Coroners Regulations 1997 regs 15, 17, 22, 22A, 23B and Schedule 3 item 2. Not encoded: the court and its officers (Part 2), s 21, s 25(1)-(3), (5), ss 26-28, 31, powers of investigation (ss 32-34), s 36 otherwise, exhumation (s 38), the conduct of inquests (Part 5, except s 44(1)-(3)), Part 6, s 62; 'person held in care' is asked as a fact; s 3 limb (d) and s 22(1)(f) are left out because the Regulations prescribe no circumstances.

roles: I am family of the person who has died
I am a doctor who was present at or soon after the death
I know of the death, and I am not family or a doctor present

situation_parameters.name: I have asked the coroner to hold an inquest
questions: May I now apply to the Supreme Court for an order that an inquest be held

situation_parameters.name: as senior next of kin, I asked the coroner not to direct a post mortem, and the coroner decided one is necessary
questions: Can the post mortem go ahead although I objected
May I still ask the Supreme Court to stop the post mortem

situation_parameters.name: a post mortem examination has been held
questions: Must the coroner write to me about the post mortem examination

situation_parameters.name: the body is under the coroner's control
questions: May I view the body while the coroner holds it
May I touch the body while the coroner holds it

qa_layer.input_parameters_note: The death is asked as four grouped inputs (where; certified; how it appears; abortion or assisted dying) and the directions as one, from which the layer builds the baseline's Death and Directions records; s 20 takes I am one of the deceased's next of kin as a BOOLEAN. So every question that may not arise for a role has at most 900 combinations of yes/no and choice inputs (NOTES, Decisions).
